newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil says European floods may hurt half.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil says European floods may hurt half.

text.p: Soft drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd said on Wednesday that floods in Europe may hurt sales in the second half of the year to December 31.
However, the company said the outlook for its business in the Philippines remained strong for the year.

"Early signs for second half results are that sales will be adversely impacted by major flooding in Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and some parts of Austria," the company said in a statement accompanying its half-year results.

C-C Amatil, 33 percent owned by The Coca-Cola Co, reported a net profit of A$58.1 million in the half year to June 30 compared with A$57.8 million a year earlier, not including Philippine operations acquired during the year.
Net profit including the Philippines was A$98.1 million.
C-C Amatil said it recorded solid operational performance in the first half of 1997, utilising its expanded geographical and distribution base and market leadership positions.
"All of the company's geographic regions increased sales volume, sales revenue and trading profit," the company said.

C-C Amatil said its Australian business recorded sound revenue and trading profit growth of three percent and six percent respectively during the period, despite an environment of very low inflation and relatively weak consumer confidence.
"Core brands achieved volume growth of three percent, building on strong growth of eight percent recorded in first half 1996," the company said.

In the Asia/Pacific, strong financial performances by the Indonesian and Papua New Guinea operations contributed to trading profit growth of 31 percent. Sales volume rose 11 percent and sales revenue grew 15 percent.
Results in New Zealand were below expectations, with profitability affected by price competition in the foodstore segment, C-C Amatil said.

C-C Amatil said the results of Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI), aquired from San Miguel Corp in a A$3.4 billion share-swap deal, had been included from April 3, the date at which the risks, benefits and control of the company effectively passed to C-C Amatil.
The combined result showed the "quantum step" C-C Amatil had made in size and profitablilty through the acquisition, it said.
On an additional 20 percent in sales revenue, trading profits had risen 43.5 percent and net operating profit almost 70 percent.
C-C Amatil also said in the three months to June 30, the Philippines operation recorded sales volume growth of 19 percent over the previous corresponding period.
Strong volume growth was achieved across the entire country.
"Whilst trading profit was below that recorded for the same period in 1996, profit margins remained strong," it said.
In Europe, the company said it posted market share gains in most of its businesses, with overall volume up 12 percent.
Sales revenue growth of two percent and trading profit growth of three percent, however, were below expectations.
Growth was affected by adverse currency movements, more subdued market conditions in Austria, Switzerland and Poland, and poor weather conditions across the region in April and June.
C-C Amatil, which is 25 percent owned by San Miguel, operates in 18 countries and is the largest Coca-Cola bottler outside the United States.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
